<jats:p>
                    The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Science</jat
title: The scientific record is never finished

We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. items.abstract: <jats:p>Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase–free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue–like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.</jats:p>
title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces

items.abstract: <jats:p>Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes
title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release

                    Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. items.abstract: <jats:p>Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. title: Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels

items.abstract: <jats:p>The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanis
title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists

items.abstract: <jats:p>Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron–containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose bal
title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation

items.abstract: <jats:p>Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metaboli
title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driv
title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling

items.abstract: <jats:p>Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.</jats:p>
title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area

items.abstract: <jats:p>Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transfo
title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress

items.abstract: <jats:p>The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours o
title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells

items.abstract: <jats:p>Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming mu
title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles

items.abstract: <jats:p>Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.</jats:p>
title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
